files.header:
=============================================================================
 Retail Application Scorecard  (RCS-APP-02)
 Owner      : Retail Credit Risk Modelling
 Purpose    : Probability of default (12m) for unsecured personal loan applications
 Developed  : 2019   Last validated: 2021-03-15
 Data       : data/processed/german_credit_{train,test}.csv  (public UCI German Credit,
              used here as a stand-in for the bank's application data)
 =============================================================================
 Method: weight-of-evidence (WoE) binning + logistic regression, scaled to points.
   1. Numeric variables with more than 10 distinct values are cut into 5 quantile bins
      (quantile type 7, breaks from the training data, outer breaks set to -Inf/Inf).
      All other variables are treated as categorical, one bin per level.
   2. WoE per bin = ln( ((n_good + 0.5) / total_good) / ((n_bad + 0.5) / total_bad) ).
      Information value IV = sum((dist_good - dist_bad) * WoE) with the same smoothing.
   3. Variables with IV >= 0.02 are kept. Protected attributes are never candidates.
   4. Logistic regression of bad (1 = default) on the WoE-transformed variables.
   5. Score = offset + factor * ln(odds_good), PDO 20, 600 points at good:bad odds 50:1.
 Usage: Rscript models/credit_scorecard/scorecard.R [data_dir] [out_dir]
 =============================================================================

purpose_and_use.text: Application PD scorecard (RCS-APP-02) estimating 12-month probability of default for unsecured personal loan applications. It is a high-tier model owned by Retail Credit Risk Modelling. The code header states the data is the public UCI German Credit set, used as a stand-in for the bank's application data, so the files provided do not show the model running on real bank data. Output is a PD and a points score per application.

evidence.quote: Purpose    : Probability of default (12m) for unsecured personal loan applications

data.text: Reads data/processed/german_credit_train.csv and german_credit_test.csv (public UCI German Credit, stand-in for bank data). Target is 'bad' (1 = default). Reference metrics show train n=700 and test n=300, each with a bad rate of 0.30, consistent with a 70/30 split of 1,000 records. How the split was made (method, seed, stratification) is not in the provided code; the split is done upstream. Excluded from candidates: id, the target, and protected attributes personal_status_sex, sex, age_group, foreign_worker. All other columns are candidate predictors. Observation window, default definition and the 12-month outcome window are not documented.

methodology.text: Weight-of-evidence binning followed by logistic regression, scaled to points. (1) Numeric variables with more than 10 distinct values are cut into 5 quantile bins (type 7, breaks from training data, outer breaks -Inf/Inf); other variables are categorical with one bin per level. (2) WoE per bin = ln(((n_good+0.5)/total_good)/((n_bad+0.5)/total_bad)), with the same 0.5 smoothing in IV. (3) Variables with IV >= 0.02 are retained; protected attributes are excluded from the candidate set. (4) Logistic regression (glm, binomial) of bad on the WoE-transformed selected variables. (5) Score = offset + factor * ln(odds_good), with PDO 20, base score 600 at good:bad odds 50:1, so factor = 20/ln2 and offset = 600 - factor*ln(50). 14 variables were selected in the reference run. CODE VS DOCUMENTATION: the 2019 methodology note describes four characteristics, 4 bins each, dummy-coded logistic regression, and scaling to 500 points at 20:1 odds with 25 PDO. The code does not match any of this, so the note is outdated and the code is taken as authoritative.

evidence.quote: Variables with IV >= 0.02 are kept. Protected attributes are never candidates.
Score = offset + factor * ln(odds_good), PDO 20, 600 points at good:bad odds 50:1.
fit <- glm(train[[TARGET]] ~ ., data = X_train, family = binomial())
The model is a logistic regression on dummy-coded bins. Scores are scaled to 500 points

implementation.text: Single R script (reference run on R 4.1.2) using only the jsonlite package; AUC, KS and Gini are hand-coded. set.seed(42) is set, although no step in the script uses random numbers. Run with: Rscript models/credit_scorecard/scorecard.R [data_dir] [out_dir], defaulting to data/processed and artifacts/reference/credit_scorecard. Outputs: bins.csv (bin-level WoE and IV), coefficients.csv (estimates and standard errors), predictions_test.csv (id, bad, pd, score), and metrics.json (parameters, selected variables, breaks and metrics). No scoring-only or production deployment code is provided.

performance.text: Reference outputs: train AUC 0.8171, Gini 0.6341, KS 0.4952 (n=700); test AUC 0.8010, Gini 0.6019, KS 0.5063 (n=300). Bad rate is 0.30 in both samples. The small train-to-test AUC drop (about 0.016) gives no sign of material overfitting on this sample. The reference outputs do not include calibration, stability (PSI), out-of-time, segment-level or fairness testing, and the test set is a hold-out, not out-of-time data. Reported figures are from the code's own calculation, not from independent validation.

monitoring_and_governance.text: Owner is Retail Credit Risk Modelling. Developed 2019; last validated 2021-03-15. The inventory classifies the model as high risk tier, which requires validation every 12 months, so validation is about 68 months overdue. Documentation is flagged as outdated: the methodology note dates from June 2019 (about 89 months old against a 24-month limit) and contradicts the code on variables, binning, model form and score scaling. No monitoring, PSI, back-testing, recalibration or change log is present in the material provided.

evidence.quote: Last independent validation: March 2021 (internal model validation team).

transformations.description: Candidates are all columns of the training data except id, bad, personal_status_sex, sex, age_group and foreign_worker.

Numeric variables with more than 10 distinct values are cut into 5 quantile bins (type 7) from training data with outer breaks set to -Inf/Inf and right-closed intervals; all other variables use one bin per level.
WoE = ln(((n_good+0.5)/total_good)/((n_bad+0.5)/total_bad)) per bin; IV is the sum of (dist_good - dist_bad)*WoE.
Variables with IV >= 0.02 are kept; 14 were selected in the reference run.
Each selected variable is replaced by the WoE of its bin; levels unseen in training receive WoE 0 (neutral).
transformations.evidence: w[is.na(w)] <- 0  # level not seen in training: neutral WoE

transformations.description: glm binomial of bad on the WoE-transformed selected variables; PD is the predicted response probability.
transformations.evidence: fit <- glm(train[[TARGET]] ~ ., data = X_train, family = binomial())

transformations.description: factor = PDO/ln(2) with PDO=20; offset = 600 - factor*ln(50); score = offset + factor*ln((1-pd)/pd).
transformations.evidence: to_score   <- function(pd) offset_pts + factor_pts * log((1 - pd) / pd)

assumptions.text: Quantile breaks and WoE/IV values estimated on the training data are assumed to remain valid for new applications.
assumptions.evidence: breaks from the training data, outer breaks set to -Inf/Inf

assumptions.text: Categories unseen in training are assumed neutral (WoE 0).
assumptions.evidence: w[is.na(w)] <- 0  # level not seen in training: neutral WoE

assumptions.text: A 0.5 additive smoothing is assumed adequate to avoid zero-count bins in WoE.
IV >= 0.02 is assumed an appropriate selection threshold; no correlation or multicollinearity screening is applied.
A linear logistic relationship on WoE values is assumed; no interaction terms are included.
assumptions.evidence: fit <- glm(train[[TARGET]] ~ ., data = X_train, family = binomial())

limitations.text: Development data is the public UCI German Credit set (stand-in), with 700 training and 300 test records, so results may not represent the bank's portfolio and sampling error is wide.
limitations.evidence: used here as a stand-in for the bank's application data

limitations.text: The methodology note materially contradicts the code (variables, bins, model form, scaling), so documentation cannot be relied on.
limitations.evidence: Each characteristic is grouped into 4 bins.

limitations.text: Validation is overdue against the 12-month high-tier requirement (last validated 2021-03-15).

The job coefficient is positive with a large standard error, and several coefficients (credit_amount, other_debtors, age, job) have wide standard errors, indicating possible collinearity or instability; no multicollinearity checks are in the code.
Age is a selected input even though age_group is treated as protected; this inconsistency needs fairness and legal review. No fairness testing is evidenced.
Only a random-style hold-out is evidenced; there is no out-of-time test, calibration assessment or reject inference, so the model reflects accepted applicants only if the data does.
